JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI Date : 04/07/2024 ORAL ORDER 1. The instant second appeal u/s 100 of the CPC is directed against the judgment and decree passed in First Appeal No.33 of 2017 by the learned appellate Court, whereby the judgment and decree delivered in Regular Civil Suit No.279 of 2014 has been reversed and the suit was decreed in favour of the original plaintiff directing the present appellant to pay damages of Rs.1,90,000/- with 9% interest from the date of the suit till realization from the date of minor Jignesh due to electrocution. 2.
texts.facts: 2.2 Legal heirs and representatives of respondent No.1 filed suit before the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge, Junagadh being Regular Civil Suit no 279/2014 claiming compensation of Rs.3 lakh. The suit was dismissed. 2.3
texts.arguments: Learned advocate for the appellant for admission of the appeal would submit that the learned appellate Court has erroneously referred and relied upon Rule 77 of the Indian Electricity Rules, 1956 (in short "the Rules") to believe that the electricity line should be hanged more than 6.1 mtr height from the ground. He would further submit that Rule 77 of the Rules is mainly applicable for the streets in the city and not in the agricultural field. He would further submit that considering the panchnama of the place at Exh.26 and considering the overall aspect, the appellant was not negligent in causing death of minor, but the minor himself, as he without remained vigilant, came in contact with 11 kv electricity line and got electrocuted, but the learned appellate Court has committed serious error in granting decree in favour of the plaintiff . 5.1 Learned advocate Mr. Dave submits to admit this appeal on the following no substantial questions of law:- "(A) Whether the Hon'ble First Appellate Court has erred in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the Hon'ble Trial Court? Learned advocate for the appellant submits that the learned appellate Court has committed serious error in interpreting Rule 77 of the Rules.
